note: Faithful rendering of the commentary on the three realities; small interpretive glosses ("ordinary" mind, dharmakaya for the suchness-body) do not change the argument.

errors.english: "Aha! You have established a meaning that was difficult to understand,"
errors.why: The teacher's would-be proud thought is in the first person: 'Aha, I have established a meaning hard to understand.'

note: Accurate account of the qualities of the Dharma teacher and the sutra list of speech qualities, apart from the person of the proud thought.

errors.english: it is of the nature of appearing to another.
errors.why: The reason clause continues on the next side ('...because there is no conceptualization in the nature of what appears to the other'); the English turns it into a positive assertion that the conceptualization has the nature of appearing to another.

note: The dialectic on determination, simultaneity and interruption of perception by conceptualization is followed well, verse included.

errors.english: Taking what is not given has been discourse continues to next page
errors.why: The Tibetan reads 'taking what is not given has, by the Blessed One, ...'; the English drops 'by the Blessed One' and inserts an editorial artefact into the text.

fix.find: has been discourse continues to next page

note: Sound rendering of the instruction on the first pārājika and the palm-tree simile; only the final line is corrupted.

errors.english:
The fourth [note: section or chapter] was composed by the Master (Drolma) Tara,
The scholar of the Eastern direction,
As a mere discourse.
errors.why: The scholar of the East (agentive ཡིས) is a separate agent who, continuing on the next side, 'does not know even a mere word' of the fourth as made by Tārā; Tārā is not the scholar, and nothing says she composed a chapter.

fix.find:
The fourth [note: section or chapter] was composed by the Master (Drolma) Tara,
The scholar of the Eastern direction,
As a mere discourse.
fix.replace:
Of the fourth as made by (Drolma) Tara,
The scholar of the East
Does not know even a mere word…

errors.english: It is not through (mudras) symbolic hand gestures or physical postures
errors.why: In this polemic about consort practice (cf. ཕྱག་རྒྱ་སྦྱོར་བ on the previous side and the union with the prajñā below), ཕྱག་རྒྱ is the karmamudrā consort, not hand gestures.

errors.english:
Since those were spoken for the sake of the students,
Why should they not also be refuted here?
errors.why: The subject is 'this [empowerment] spoken of with regard to the disciple': why should it too not be refuted by the arguments the Pramāṇavārttika used; it is not a reason clause about earlier teachings.

note: The verse sequence is followed, but the polemic against consort-based empowerment is blurred and the closing lines misattribute who does what.

errors.english: Because there is no ignorance separate from the different actions.
errors.why: ལས here is the ablative continuing བདག from the previous side: 'because there is no ignorance different from the self'; there are no 'actions'.

fix.find: Because there is no ignorance separate from the different actions.
fix.replace: Because there is no ignorance different from [the self].

errors.english: the view of a self (satkayadrishti) the view of a personal identity
errors.why: The verse has སེམས་ཅན་ལྟ་བ, the view of a 'being' (sattvadṛṣṭi), not འཇིག་ཚོགས་ལ་ལྟ་བ (satkāyadṛṣṭi).

note: The refutation of the Vedāntin/Mīmāṃsaka self is mostly clear, but the opening is mistranslated and the Pramāṇavārttika verse is flattened into prose with a wrong term.

errors.english: it is not expressed as being "possessed of the very basis upon which that basis is obtained," which refers to its essential nature
errors.why: No negation: the citation 'one possesses that very basis which one has obtained' is evidently to be read as 'that very essence', illustrating vastu = svabhāva.

fix.find: it is not expressed as being "possessed of the very basis upon which that basis is obtained," which refers to its essential nature
fix.replace: in the statement "one possesses that very basis which one has obtained," the meaning is evidently "that very essence"

errors.why: ཀུན་ཏུ་སྦྱོར་བ is saṃyojana, the fetters; glossing it as proclivities/latent afflictions confuses it with the anuśayas.

note: The five senses of vastu and the karmadhāraya analysis of upādāna-skandha are followed well apart from an inserted negation in the first example.
Faithful rendering of the chapter end, colophon and the first signs of irreversibility; the large-number series is approximate but harmless.

errors.why: The rule is that the final h of a root beginning with d becomes gh; it is the h of duh, not the initial d, that becomes gh (the d becomes dh in the next step).

note: The grammatical derivations are tracked closely; a few transliterations of examples are slightly off and one sound change is assigned to the wrong segment.

errors.english: When butter is poured from the ladle, the flames should take the shapes of a trident
errors.why: The verse lists 'the shape of the butter-oblation ladle' as one of the auspicious flame shapes; it is not a temporal clause about pouring.

note: A good, readable rendering of the fire-sign verses and the obstacle-removal procedure, verse recast as prose.
